programmes.funder: ACT Government (Chief Minister, Treasury and Economic Development Directorate)
programmes.amount_note: Matched grants of up to A$30,000 (dollar-for-dollar) to help Canberra-based entrepreneurs develop and commercialise innovative products and services.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs in rounds, historically two rounds per year, each open for several weeks.
programmes.reopen_note: Innovation Connect has run in repeated rounds for over a decade. Check the ACT Government business grants page for the next round.

procedure_steps.detail: Attend an ACT Government pre-application briefing or speak to a business adviser.
Submit the application with project plan and matched funding evidence during an open round.
Panel assessment and pitch where required.
Grant agreement and acquittal.

documents_required.doc: ABN and evidence of ACT operations

eligibility.other_note: Canberra-based individuals or businesses with an innovative product or service. Applicants must be able to match the grant with their own funds.

programmes.source_snippet: Innovation Connect grants help Canberra businesses develop and commercialise innovative products and services.

programmes.amount_note: ARENA's flagship open programme; grant size is set per project and negotiated. Supports development, demonstration and pre-commercial deployment.
programmes.deadline_note: Ongoing open programme with expressions of interest accepted continuously.

procedure_steps.detail: Discuss the project concept with ARENA
Submit an expression of interest through the ARENA portal
If invited, submit a full application
ARENA board decision and funding agreement

eligibility.other_note: Applicants generally need an Australian entity and a project delivered in Australia.

programmes.source_snippet: supports a range of development, demonstration and pre-commercial deployment

programmes.amount_note: AUD 523.2 million programme to support Australian battery manufacturing across priority segments.
programmes.deadline_note: Listed as closed on the ARENA funding page.
programmes.reopen_note: No successor round announced at the time of checking. Battery manufacturing remains supported under the Future Made in Australia Innovation Fund.
programmes.source_snippet: Battery Breakthrough Initiative: $523.2 million, Closed

programmes.amount_note: Up to AUD 1.1 billion in grant funding to support development of a domestic low-carbon liquid fuels industry.
programmes.deadline_note: Listed by ARENA as in development at the time of checking; guidelines not yet published.
programmes.reopen_note: Programme is in development. Watch arena.gov.au/funding for the first round guidelines.
programmes.source_snippet: up to $1.1 billion in grant funding to support the development of a domestic

programmes.amount_note: Grants to demonstrate and deploy zero emissions vehicle technology and refuelling or charging infrastructure. Amounts set per project.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered through funding rounds announced on the ARENA funding page.
programmes.source_snippet: enable the demonstration and deployment of new zero emissions vehicle

programmes.amount_note: ARENA provides grant funding for renewable energy and decarbonisation technology projects from early-stage R&D through to large demonstration. Amounts range from a few hundred thousand dollars for feasibility studies to tens or hundreds of millions for demonstration plants. Co-funding of at least 50% is typically expected and ARENA funding is generally milestone-based.
programmes.deadline_note: ARENA runs specific competitive funding rounds (for example hydrogen, electrolyser, industrial decarbonisation and community battery rounds) each with its own opening and closing dates, alongside an advancing renewables pathway for unsolicited applications.
programmes.reopen_note: ARENA continuously opens new targeted funding rounds. Founders should subscribe to ARENA funding alerts, since individual rounds are open for only a few months and are heavily oversubscribed.

procedure_steps.detail: Review currently open ARENA funding rounds and the advancing renewables pathway.
Discuss the project concept with ARENA staff before applying.
Submit an expression of interest or full application via the ARENA portal.
Assessment against merit criteria including technology readiness, knowledge-sharing value and co-funding.
Board approval and execution of a funding agreement with milestone payments and knowledge-sharing obligations.

documents_required.doc: Environmental and planning approvals for deployment projects

eligibility.other_note: Entities with an ABN, generally incorporated in Australia. Projects must be delivered in Australia and relate to renewable energy or enabling decarbonisation technologies. Knowledge sharing with the sector is a condition of funding.

programmes.source_snippet: ARENA provides funding to accelerate the development of renewable energy and related technologies in Australia.

programmes.name_local: Future Made in Australia Innovation Fund
programmes.name_en: Future Made in Australia Innovation Fund
programmes.amount_note: Up to AUD 1.5 billion in grant funding across priority net-zero industries including green metals, low-carbon liquid fuels, clean energy manufacturing and battery supply chains.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered through sequential streams and rounds announced by ARENA.
programmes.source_snippet: provide up to $1.5 billion in grant funding

programmes.amount_note: Revenue support (production credit) covering the commercial gap for large-scale renewable hydrogen production, paid per kilogram over up to ten years.
programmes.deadline_note: Round 2 is listed as closed on the ARENA funding page.
programmes.reopen_note: Two rounds have been run to date. Any Round 3 would be announced through ARENA; the programme is aimed at very large projects rather than early-stage startups.
programmes.source_snippet: Hydrogen Headstart Round 2: Closed (revenue support for hydrogen production)

programmes.name_local: Powering the Regions Fund - Industrial Transformation Stream
programmes.name_en: Powering the Regions Fund Industrial Transformation Stream
programmes.amount_note: AUD 400 million announced in the 2023-24 Federal Budget to decarbonise existing industrial facilities and develop new clean energy industries in the regions.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered through streams and rounds announced by ARENA.
programmes.source_snippet: In the 2023-24 Federal Budget, the Australian Government announced $400 million

programmes.amount_note: Grants for manufacturing facilities across the solar photovoltaic supply chain in Australia. Round budgets are announced per stream.
programmes.deadline_note: Delivered in rounds; check the ARENA funding page for the currently open stream.
programmes.source_snippet: Solar Sunshot - Open - Focus: Manufacturing facilities across the solar supply chain

programmes.name_local: Ultra Low-Cost Solar PV Research and Development
programmes.name_en: ARENA Ultra Low-Cost Solar PV R&D funding round
programmes.amount_note: AUD 60 million round supporting research and development towards ARENA's Solar 30 30 30 target (30% module efficiency and 30 cents per watt installed by 2030).
programmes.deadline_note: Listed as closed on the ARENA funding page.
programmes.reopen_note: ARENA has run repeated solar R&D rounds; monitor arena.gov.au/funding for the next one.
programmes.source_snippet: Ultra Low-Cost Solar PV R&D: $60 million, Closed

programmes.amount_note: Market-entry programme providing a period of operational support in overseas innovation hubs, including access to co-working space, local market advisers, investor and customer introductions. No cash grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications for placement in the Landing Pad locations, subject to capacity.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose the target Landing Pad location.
Submit the online application with the market-entry plan.
Assessment interview with the Landing Pad manager.
Placement and structured market-entry support.

eligibility.other_note: Market-ready Australian scale-ups with a validated product, evidence of traction and the resources to commit to overseas market entry.

programmes.source_snippet: Landing Pads help Australian scale-ups access global innovation hubs and international markets.

programmes.funder: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (AusIndustry)
programmes.amount_note: Grants of A$100,000 to A$3 million over up to three years for short-term industry-led collaborative research. Funding covers up to 50% of eligible project costs and the project must include at least two Australian industry entities (one of which is an SME) and at least one Australian research organisation.
programmes.deadline_note: Competitive rounds announced periodically by the Department. Rounds are open for roughly six to eight weeks each.
programmes.reopen_note: CRC-P has historically run one or more competitive rounds per year, though the timing has become irregular. Check business.gov.au and GrantConnect for the next round; the broader CRC Program (long-term centres) also runs separate annual selection rounds.

procedure_steps.detail: Assemble the consortium: at least two Australian industry entities including one SME, and at least one Australian research organisation.
Agree the collaboration terms, IP arrangements and cash and in-kind contributions.
Submit the application via the business.gov.au portal during an open round.
Merit assessment by an independent committee.
If successful, execute the grant agreement and the consortium agreement before project start.

documents_required.doc: Signed letters of support from all partners
Budget including cash and in-kind contributions from each partner
Draft consortium agreement and IP arrangements

eligibility.other_note: The lead applicant must be an Australian entity with an ABN, incorporated and trading in Australia. Projects must be industry-led and collaborative, and must not have already commenced.

programmes.source_snippet: CRC-P grants support short-term, industry-led collaborative research projects.

programmes.funder: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO)
programmes.amount_note: 'Access up to 2 vouchers between $20K - $60K each', matched dollar-for-dollar by the business ('$60,000 from CSIRO = $60,000 from the business'). Vouchers pay for CSIRO research services on a 2-12 month project.
programmes.deadline_note: No fixed rounds published on the eligibility page; applications are made when a suitable project is scoped with CSIRO.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm eligibility (turnover/trading history, GST registration, ACN or ICN, ability to match funding).
Scope a 2-12 month R&D project requiring scientific, technical or analytical expertise with CSIRO.
Submit the Kick-Start application and, if successful, contract the research with CSIRO.

documents_required.doc: Kick-Start application form with project scope
Evidence of ACN/ICN and GST registration
Evidence of turnover/operating expenditure or trading history

eligibility.other_note: Must either have 'annual turnover and operating expenditure under $10 million' OR 'have been trading for less than three years'; must 'be registered for GST' and 'hold an Australian Company Number (ACN) or Indigenous Corporation Number (ICN)'; must provide the matching cash contribution. 'International companies and Australian subsidiaries of international companies are not eligible.'

programmes.source_snippet: Access up to 2 vouchers between $20K - $60K each ... $60,000 from CSIRO = $60,000 from the business ... annual turnover and operating expenditure under $10 million ... have been trading for less than three years.

programmes.name_en: CSIRO ON Innovation Program (ON Prime / ON Accelerate)
programmes.amount_note: ON Prime is a pre-accelerator that provides structured customer-discovery training with no cash grant. ON Accelerate cohorts have historically provided a cash allowance to participating teams alongside intensive commercialisation coaching. Availability and cash components vary by cohort.
programmes.deadline_note: Cohort-based, with applications opening for each ON Prime or ON Accelerate intake. Historically one to two cohorts per year.
programmes.reopen_note: CSIRO has periodically restructured its ON programme portfolio. Check the CSIRO innovation programs page for the current cohort structure and next intake, as programme names and formats have changed between cycles.

procedure_steps.detail: Form a team including a technical lead and a business lead.
Apply during an open cohort call.
Selection interview.
Participate in the multi-week customer discovery and commercialisation programme.
Pitch at the cohort showcase.

documents_required.doc: Description of the research or technology
Institutional support letter where the team is university- or CSIRO-based

eligibility.other_note: Open to research teams from CSIRO, Australian universities and publicly funded research organisations, and in some cohorts to early-stage deep tech companies.

programmes.source_snippet: CSIRO's innovation programs help researchers and entrepreneurs turn science into impact.

programmes.amount_note: Grant amounts differ by tier and are set in the guidelines for each round; no amount is published on the current programme page, so none is recorded here. Four streams exist: Tier 1 (SMEs ready to export), Tier 2 (exporting within existing markets), Tier 3 (exporting to new key markets) and representative bodies.
programmes.deadline_note: No round is open at the time of verification: 'Currently there are no grant rounds open to applications' and 'EMDG Round 4 is closed'. Austrade states 'We will update our website when timing of the next grant round is confirmed.' The programme runs in recurring multi-year rounds.

procedure_steps.detail: Check eligibility and read the EMDG guidelines and legislation.
Wait for the next grant round to open and apply through the Austrade grants portal.
If successful, enter a multi-year grant agreement and acquit eligible marketing/promotion and export training expenses.

documents_required.note: Available only while a round is open

documents_required.doc: Evidence of eligible export promotion expenditure and export plan

eligibility.other_note: 'The EMDG program provides grants to Australian small and medium enterprises and their representative bodies to: market and promote their goods and services globally [and] undertake export training.' Turnover ceilings and tier tests are defined in the round guidelines, which we did not read.

programmes.source_snippet: The EMDG program provides grants to Australian small and medium enterprises and their representative bodies to: market and promote their goods and services globally ... Currently there are no grant rounds open to applications.

programmes.funder: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
programmes.amount_note: Early-stage commercialisation and growth grants of A$50,000 to A$5 million, matched on a 50:50 basis, plus free specialist advisory services from an Industry Growth Program adviser. Grants targeted at priority areas of the National Reconstruction Fund.
programmes.deadline_note: business.gov.au states: 'This program is currently paused to new applications.' The pause applies to new grant applications; existing grant agreements and adviser engagements continue.
programmes.reopen_note: No reopening date has been published by the Department of Industry, Science and Resources as at 14 August 2026. The pause was applied without a public announcement and was reported in the trade press in 2025-26. Founders should monitor the business.gov.au programme page and the Department's Industry Growth Program page for any resumption, and in the meantime consider the R&D Tax Incentive, ARENA, MRFF and state-level commercialisation grants as substitutes.

procedure_steps.detail: Check business.gov.au for resumption of applications before investing effort.
When open, request an Industry Growth Program adviser engagement to assess commercialisation readiness.
Adviser prepares a recommendation supporting a grant application.
Submit the grant application through the business.gov.au portal.
Assessment against merit criteria and, if successful, execution of a grant agreement with milestone payments.

documents_required.doc: Detailed budget with matched funding evidence
Financial statements for the last two years
Evidence of Australian incorporation and ABN

eligibility.other_note: Australian incorporated SMEs with an ABN, fewer than 200 employees, operating in one of the National Reconstruction Fund priority areas. Applicants must be able to fund 50% of project costs from other sources.

programmes.source_snippet: This program is currently paused to new applications.

programmes.funder: Department of Health, Disability and Ageing / National Health and Medical Research Council (administering)
programmes.amount_note: A A$20 billion endowment funding health and medical research and innovation through targeted competitive grant opportunities. Individual grants range from a few hundred thousand dollars to tens of millions depending on the initiative. Relevant streams for companies include the Biomedical Translation Bridge and BioMedTech Horizons style initiatives, plus targeted translational research missions.
programmes.deadline_note: Individual grant opportunities are published on GrantConnect with their own closing dates. The MRFF publishes a rolling implementation plan setting out upcoming opportunities.
programmes.reopen_note: The MRFF is a permanent endowment with new grant opportunities released continuously under 10-year investment plans. Register for GrantConnect notifications filtered to MRFF to catch relevant opportunities, since individual rounds are typically open for six to ten weeks.

procedure_steps.detail: Monitor GrantConnect and the MRFF implementation plan for relevant opportunities.
Identify whether an administering institution (university, MRI or hospital) is required as the lead applicant.
Prepare the application in Sapphire or the relevant grants system.
Peer review and assessment.
Award and execution of the funding agreement.

eligibility.other_note: Eligibility varies by grant opportunity. Many streams require an Australian university, medical research institute or hospital as administering institution; some translation and commercialisation streams admit companies directly or as partners.

programmes.source_snippet: The Medical Research Future Fund is a long-term investment supporting Australian health and medical research.

programmes.amount_note: A A$15 billion investment vehicle providing loans, guarantees and equity (not grants) on commercial or concessional terms into seven priority areas. Individual investments are typically A$5 million and above; the NRFC co-invests with private capital rather than acting as a sole funder.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling. Investment proposals are submitted through the NRFC website and assessed on a commercial basis; there is no application round.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the project falls within one of the seven priority areas (renewables and low emissions technologies, medical science, transport, value-add in agriculture forestry and fisheries, value-add in resources, defence capability, enabling capabilities).
Submit an investment enquiry through the NRFC website with a summary of the opportunity.
Initial screening and, if progressed, detailed due diligence.
Investment committee and board approval.
Documentation and funding.

documents_required.doc: Details of co-investors and capital structure
Technical and market due diligence material

eligibility.other_note: Australian businesses seeking growth or project finance in the seven NRFC priority areas. Not suitable for pre-revenue seed-stage companies; the NRFC targets investable propositions with commercial returns.

programmes.source_snippet: The National Reconstruction Fund Corporation provides finance to diversify and transform Australian industry.

programmes.amount_note: Matched grants of A$25,000 to A$50,000 covering up to 50% of eligible costs to take a proof of concept to a minimum viable product and towards first customers.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs in competitive rounds rather than continuously. Rounds have historically opened once or twice a year and closed quickly once the funding pool is committed.
programmes.reopen_note: Check the NSW Government grants and funding page for the next MVP Ventures round. NSW also runs the Minimum Viable Product and Techvouchers programmes; where MVP Ventures is closed, Techvouchers and the Physical Sciences Fund may be open.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the technology has completed proof of concept and is ready for MVP development.
Register in the NSW grants portal during an open round.
Submit the application with project plan, budget and evidence of matched funding.
Assessment against merit criteria.
Grant agreement and milestone-based payment.

documents_required.doc: Project plan and MVP development milestones
Evidence of NSW operations and ABN
Evidence of the completed proof of concept

eligibility.other_note: NSW-based companies with an ABN, generally with limited revenue and fewer than a specified number of employees, that have completed a proof of concept and are developing a minimum viable product.

programmes.source_snippet: The MVP Ventures Program helps NSW startups take an innovative product from proof of concept to minimum viable product.

programmes.amount_note: Matched vouchers of up to A$50,000 (dollar-for-dollar) for NSW SMEs to collaborate with a NSW publicly funded research organisation on a research and development project.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs in rounds; applications close when the round's funding is exhausted.
programmes.reopen_note: TechVouchers has run in repeated rounds under the NSW Physical Sciences Fund and related programmes. Check the NSW grants portal for the current round.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify a NSW publicly funded research organisation partner and scope the project.
Obtain a quotation and letter of support from the research partner.
Apply through the NSW grants portal during an open round.
Assessment and, if successful, grant agreement and project delivery.

documents_required.doc: Project scope agreed with the research partner
Research partner quotation and support letter
ABN and evidence of NSW operations

eligibility.other_note: NSW-based SMEs partnering with a NSW publicly funded research organisation.

programmes.source_snippet: TechVouchers support NSW SMEs to work with research organisations on innovation projects.

programmes.name_local: Business Boost and Business Growth Fund (Queensland)
programmes.name_en: Queensland Business Boost and Business Growth Fund
programmes.funder: Department of Customer Services, Open Data and Small and Family Business (Queensland Government)
programmes.amount_note: Business Boost provides grants of around A$15,000 for small business capability projects; the Business Growth Fund provides up to A$50,000 for specialised equipment to enable high-growth businesses to scale. Both are matched-funding programmes.
programmes.deadline_note: Both programmes run in short competitive rounds that have historically closed within days of opening due to demand, sometimes using a registration-of-interest ballot.
programmes.reopen_note: Queensland small business grants are re-announced each state budget cycle with varying names and quantum. Monitor business.qld.gov.au grants finder and register for alerts, since rounds close extremely quickly.

procedure_steps.detail: Register for Queensland business grant alerts.
When a round opens, submit the application immediately with quotations.
Assessment against eligibility and merit criteria.
Grant agreement and acquittal.

documents_required.doc: ABN and evidence of Queensland operations
Payroll evidence to demonstrate employee numbers

eligibility.other_note: Queensland-based small businesses meeting turnover and employee thresholds that vary by programme and round.

programmes.source_snippet: The Queensland Government offers a range of grants to help small businesses start, grow and employ.

programmes.funder: Department of State Development, Infrastructure and Planning (Advance Queensland)
programmes.amount_note: Grants of up to A$200,000 across tiers (historically Tier 1 up to A$100,000 and Tier 2 up to A$200,000) to commercialise a product, process or service that is at minimum viable product stage or beyond. Applicants must contribute matched funding.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs in competitive rounds, historically one round per year, open for around four to six weeks.
programmes.reopen_note: Ignite Ideas has run for multiple rounds since 2015 under Advance Queensland. Check the Advance Queensland website for the next round; the programme has been subject to changes in scope and funding under successive Queensland budgets.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the product is at MVP stage or beyond with evidence of market validation.
Register on the Queensland grants portal when a round opens.
Submit the application with commercialisation plan, budget and evidence of matched funding.
Assessment by an independent panel.
Grant agreement and milestone reporting.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of MVP and market validation
ABN and evidence of Queensland operations
Letters of support from customers or partners

eligibility.other_note: Queensland-headquartered small and medium businesses with fewer than 200 employees, with a product at MVP stage or beyond.

programmes.source_snippet: The Ignite Ideas Fund supports Queensland small and medium businesses to commercialise innovative products and services.

programmes.funder: Department of Industry, Science and Resources (AusIndustry) jointly with the Australian Taxation Office
programmes.amount_note: A tax offset that 'offset[s] some of the costs you put into eligible research and development'. Offset rates and turnover thresholds are set in tax law and are not stated on this landing page — we did not verify a rate, so none is recorded here. The Government announced changes to the R&DTI in the 2026-27 Budget which 'will start from 1 July 2028. Until then, the program will continue running under the current rules.'
programmes.deadline_note: Registration of R&D activities is made after the end of each income year, within a statutory deadline (10 months after the end of the income year under the current rules — not verified on this page). The programme is ongoing and recurring each income year.

procedure_steps.detail: Self-assess whether your company and its R&D activities meet the eligibility requirements.
Optionally apply for an advance finding (certainty about activity eligibility) or an overseas finding (for activities conducted outside Australia).
Conduct and document core and supporting R&D activities.
Register the activities through the R&DTI customer portal, then claim the offset in the company tax return with the ATO.

documents_required.doc: Contemporaneous records evidencing core and supporting R&D activities and expenditure
Company income tax return with R&D tax offset schedule (ATO)

documents_required.note: Only where certainty is sought or activities are conducted overseas

eligibility.other_note: Open to companies conducting eligible core and supporting R&D activities. Some activities are excluded; a registered research service provider may conduct R&D on your behalf.

programmes.source_snippet: Offset some of the costs you put into eligible research and development. ... The Australian Government announced changes to the R&DTI in the 2026–27 Budget. These changes will start from 1 July 2028. Until then, the program will continue running under the current rules.

programmes.name_local: Research, Commercialisation and Startup Fund (South Australia)
programmes.name_en: South Australian Research, Commercialisation and Startup Fund (RCSF)
programmes.funder: Department of State Development (South Australian Government)
programmes.amount_note: Grants across streams covering early-stage commercialisation and startup support, with individual awards historically from around A$50,000 to A$500,000 depending on the stream, generally with matched funding required.
programmes.deadline_note: Competitive rounds announced by the South Australian Government, typically annually.
programmes.reopen_note: The RCSF has run in successive rounds since 2021. Monitor the South Australian Department of State Development website and business.sa.gov.au for the next round announcement.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the project aligns with a current RCSF stream.
Apply through the South Australian grants portal when a round opens.
Merit assessment.
Grant agreement and milestone-based payments.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of South Australian operations and ABN
Research partner support letter where applicable

eligibility.other_note: South Australian-based startups, researchers and SMEs commercialising research or novel technology.

programmes.source_snippet: The Research, Commercialisation and Startup Fund supports the translation of South Australian research into new companies and products.

programmes.amount_note: Games Expansion Pack funding supports Australian game development studios with production grants; funding caps are set in the current guidelines. Screen Australia also administers the Digital Games Tax Offset eligibility certificates.
programmes.deadline_note: Rounds are announced on the Screen Australia games funding page with fixed closing dates.

eligibility.other_note: Australian companies; the Digital Games Tax Offset provides a separate refundable tax offset on qualifying Australian development expenditure.

programmes.funder: Enterprize Tasmania (supported by the Tasmanian Government)
programmes.amount_note: Tasmania's startup hub, providing pre-accelerator and accelerator programmes, coworking space and small seed grants or stipends to participating founders. Cash amounts vary by programme and are typically modest.
programmes.deadline_note: Cohort programmes are advertised on the Enterprize website with their own application windows; hub membership is rolling.

procedure_steps.detail: Review the current Enterprize programmes.
Apply to the relevant cohort or become a hub member.
Selection interview.
Participate in the programme.

eligibility.other_note: Tasmanian founders and startups, or those willing to base themselves in Tasmania.

programmes.source_snippet: Enterprize is Tasmania's startup hub, supporting founders from idea to investment.

programmes.amount_note: A A$2 billion, ten-year investment fund making equity and equity-like investments into Victorian research translation and scale-up companies. Cheque sizes typically range from a few hundred thousand dollars for early-stage translation to tens of millions for scale-ups. Not a grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling. Investment enquiries are submitted through the Breakthrough Victoria website and assessed on a commercial basis.

procedure_steps.detail: Submit an investment enquiry through the Breakthrough Victoria website.
Initial screening call and assessment of the Victorian nexus.
Due diligence including technical, commercial and financial review.
Investment committee approval.
Documentation and funding, usually alongside co-investors.

documents_required.doc: Details of co-investors and round structure

eligibility.other_note: Companies with a substantive Victorian presence or willing to establish one, in the fund's priority sectors: health and life sciences, agri-food, clean economy, digital technologies and advanced manufacturing.

programmes.source_snippet: Breakthrough Victoria invests in Victorian innovation to create jobs and grow the state's economy.

programmes.amount_note: LaunchVic funds accelerators, pre-accelerators and ecosystem initiatives rather than making direct grants to most startups. Startups access support by joining a LaunchVic-funded programme (for example Alice Anderson Fund for women-led ventures, and sector accelerators). Some direct founder programmes include stipends.
programmes.deadline_note: LaunchVic issues periodic calls for programme delivery partners; startups apply to individual funded programmes on those programmes' own timelines.
programmes.reopen_note: LaunchVic's funding calls change with each Victorian budget cycle. The Alice Anderson Fund (co-investment into women-led startups) and sector-specific accelerators operate on independent timetables.

procedure_steps.detail: Browse the LaunchVic programmes directory for currently open accelerators and initiatives.
Apply directly to the relevant programme operator.
For delivery partners, respond to LaunchVic's funding calls when open.

eligibility.other_note: Victorian-based founders and startups. Several LaunchVic initiatives specifically target women founders, First Nations founders and regional Victoria.

programmes.source_snippet: LaunchVic invests in programs and initiatives that strengthen Victoria's startup ecosystem.

programmes.funder: Department of Jobs, Tourism, Science and Innovation (Western Australia)
programmes.amount_note: Grants of up to A$40,000 to help WA startups and SMEs develop and commercialise innovative products and services, delivered under the New Industries Fund.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs in competitive rounds under the New Industries Fund, typically once or twice a year.
programmes.reopen_note: The New Industries Fund umbrella has been re-scoped across WA budget cycles. Check the WA Department of Jobs, Tourism, Science and Innovation website for the current suite, which has included the Innovation Booster Grant, New Industries Fund Innovation Seed Fund and Female Innovators Boost.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the innovation is at a stage suitable for the grant's technology readiness requirements.
Apply through the WA grants portal during an open round.
Assessment by an independent panel.
Grant agreement and milestone reporting.

documents_required.doc: ABN and evidence of WA operations

eligibility.other_note: Western Australian-based startups and small businesses. Some rounds have had dedicated allocations for female founders and regional applicants.

programmes.source_snippet: The New Industries Fund supports the growth and development of new and emerging businesses in Western Australia.
